transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?
I guess it’s what I feel afterward. I’ll be sitting there looking at all the empty containers, and I just feel disgusted with myself. Like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be.
Can you tell me what's in those containers you find yourself surrounded by afterward?

Usually it’s pozole. I’ll heat up what I tell myself is one bowl, then I’ve eaten the whole pot—plus a couple of tamales, chips, whatever leftovers are there. It’s like I was feeding a whole crew, not just me.
After you eat this much, do you do anything afterward to try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot?
I’m not sure what you mean by making up for it. I just… after I eat, I feel bad about it.
How often would you say these episodes of eating much more than you planned happen—like, how many times per week, and for how many months has this been going on?
Since I’ve been home with my back injury, it’s been several nights most weeks. It’s been about three months now, and I can’t think of a week where it didn’t happen at least once.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?
Yeah. Once I start, it’s like the discipline I had on the road just shuts off. Even when I’m telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down,” I keep going back for more.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating objectively large amounts of food (whole pot of pozole plus additional items) with a subjective loss of control, occurring at least once weekly for approximately 3 months, associated with marked distress and self-disgust afterward. No compensatory behaviors (vomiting, laxative use, excessive exercise) are present, ruling out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). While the frequency and duration approach full Binge-Eating Disorder criteria, only one associated feature (marked distress/disgust) was explicitly confirmed, without corroboration of other criteria such as eating rapidly, eating until uncomfortably full, eating alone due to embarrassment, or eating despite not being physically hungry. Given this partial symptom profile, the presentation is best classified as an Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (F50.8), consistent with atypical/subthreshold Binge-Eating Disorder.
